newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end down on portfolio reshuffling.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end down on portfolio reshuffling.

text.p: Greek equities closed down and brokers said the market was dominated by nervous sentiment and portfolio reshuffling while awaiting the 1997 budget.

"Predominant nervous market sentiment has kept investors on the sidelines," said Emmanuel Varsos, managing director at Investment Analysis SA. "Portfolio reshuffling by institutionals is the dominant feature of a market that awaits the announcement of the 1997 budget."
Varsos said he expected the benchmark index to hover around 950 points until the 1997 budget was submitted to parliament at the end of next month.
"The fall effect and the Monday effect also contributed to today's retreat," he said. "Historical price data show that falling sessions outnumber rising sessions by three to one on Mondays."
The Athens general share index closed 0.70 percent, or 6.76 points lower at 954.11 from Friday's 951.43 close after opening at 960.41 points.
Turnover was at 6.08 billion drachmas on volume of 5.24 million shares.

Gainers traced decliners 54 to 151 with 29 issues unchanged on 234 traded. Banks fell 0.94 percent, industrials down 0.75 percent and construction ended lower 1.12 percent. Small-caps fell 1.87 percent.
